result.summary: Prevents wallet fee-bumped transactions from receiving a locktime older than the transaction they replace. When `bumpfee` creates a replacement transaction, the original transaction's locktime is passed to `DiscourageFeeSniping` as a lower bound, constraining random anti-fee-sniping backdating to the range between the previous locktime and the chain tip.
result.problem: Bitcoin Core's anti-fee-sniping logic randomly backdates transaction locktimes by up to 99 blocks approximately 10% of the time. When bumping fees, this random backdating can cause a replacement transaction to have an earlier locktime than the original, creating an unnatural on-chain pattern that acts as a fingerprint identifying Bitcoin Core or Electrum wallets.
evidence: Closes issue #26526 ('Wallet: Don't backdate locktime rbf').

PR author's empirical analysis of over 1,000,000 RBF transactions between May 2025 and June 2026 found 200-300 backdated replacements per week (<2% of all replacements), concluding that 'the few transactions that do exhibit backdating are easily fingerprintable as having been replaced using bumpfee in Bitcoin Core or Electrum.'
result.card: This PR modifies wallet fee bumping to prevent replacement transactions from having an nLockTime older than the transaction being replaced. Bitcoin Core's anti-fee-sniping feature randomly backdates transaction locktimes by up to 99 blocks about 10% of the time, which during bumpfee can set a locktime earlier than the original transaction. This anomaly serves as an on-chain fingerprint identifying Bitcoin Core and Electrum wallets. Empirical analysis cited in the PR found roughly 200 to 300 such backdated replacements per week across over one million surveyed RBF transactions.

risk.why: A flaw in anti-fee-sniping bounds calculation could set an unintended locktime, temporarily delaying transaction confirmation for users bumping fees.
